title: Add a task from the document bar
prompt:
# Story: Add a task from the document bar

- **Story**: XXX-add-task
- **Created**: 2026-11-28
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open a story, press Add task, write a task and press Enter; reload and see it still there; edit it with its pencil; delete
  another one with its bin; see the dot on Sync; sync and see the tasks in the story's `meta.json` on GitHub while `story.md` is unchanged.

## Story

As a team member, I want to add a task to an open story from its bar, and to edit or delete any of its tasks from the task's own row, so
that the story always lists the work a pair must do to deliver it, kept with the story without having to edit its text.

## Acceptance tests

The Add task button

- [ ] **Given** an open story, **Then** the bar shows "Add task" with a plus icon as its first button, with the hint "Add a task to this
  story".
- [ ] **Given** an open architectural enabler, driver or ADR, **Then** there is no Add task button.

Adding a task

- [ ] **Given** an open story, **When** the user presses Add task, **Then** a field labelled "New task", with the placeholder "Describe the
  task", opens below the task list, gets the focus, and is scrolled into view, with a "Save task" button (check) and a "Cancel" button
  (cross).
- [ ] **Given** a story with no task, **When** the user presses Add task, **Then** the section "Tasks 0" shows with the field.
- [ ] **Given** the field is empty or holds only spaces, **Then** "Save task" is disabled and Enter does nothing.
- [ ] **Given** the field holds a text, **When** the user presses Enter or "Save task", **Then** the task is added at the end of the list
  with the text trimmed, the count goes up by one, and the field closes.
- [ ] **Given** the field is open, **When** the user presses Escape or "Cancel", **Then** the field closes and nothing is added.
- [ ] **Given** the user pressed Add task and then the pencil of a task, **Then** the new-task field closes and only the edited row is a
  field.

Each task has Edit and Delete

- [ ] **Given** a story with tasks, **Then** the section shows "Tasks" and their count, and each task is a row with its text (long text
  wraps), an "Update task" button (pencil) and a "Remove task" button (bin). Their accessible names are "Update task: <text>" and "Remove
  task: <text>".
- [ ] **When** the user presses the pencil of a task, **Then** the row becomes a field labelled "Edit task" holding the text of the task,
  focused, with "Save task" and "Cancel". Only one task is edited at a time.
- [ ] **Given** the edited text is not empty, **When** the user presses Enter or "Save task", **Then** the row shows the new text, trimmed,
  in the same place in the list.
- [ ] **Given** the edited text is empty, **Then** "Save task" is disabled. Emptying a task does not delete it; the bin does.
- [ ] **When** the user presses Escape or "Cancel" while editing, **Then** the row shows its text as it was.
- [ ] **When** the user presses the bin of a task, **Then** the task is removed at once, without a confirmation, and the count goes down
  by one. If it was being edited, the edit ends.
- [ ] **Given** the last task is removed and no field is open, **Then** the Tasks section is hidden.

A task is stored with the story at once

- [ ] **Given** the user added, edited or removed a task, **Then** the story's tasks are stored in the project's database at once, without
  pressing Save, and no request is made to GitHub.
- [ ] **Given** the user added a task, **When** the page is reloaded or the story is closed and opened again, **Then** the task is there,
  with the same text and in the same order.
- [ ] **Given** the text of the story has unsaved changes, **When** the user adds a task, **Then** the task is stored and the text keeps its
  unsaved changes; Save still stores the text.
- [ ] **Given** the user added, edited or removed a task, **Then** the Markdown text of the story is unchanged.
- [ ] **Given** the story's tasks differ from what was last synced, **Then** the Sync button has its dot and the hint "Saved here, not on
  GitHub yet. Sync to push it."

The tasks of the text and the tasks of the list

- [ ] **Given** a story created by the AI, **Then** its task list holds the tasks written under its `## Tasks`, in order (top-level items,
  bulleted or numbered, with or without a checkbox, up to the next heading or horizontal rule).
- [ ] **Given** the user saves the text and its `## Tasks` gained a task, **Then** that task is added at the end of the list. A task that is
  already in the list (same text, ignoring case and extra spaces) is not added twice.
- [ ] **Given** the user removed a task from the list, **When** the text is saved again without that line changing, **Then** the task does
  not come back.

On GitHub

- [ ] **Given** a story with tasks, **When** it is synced, **Then** its `meta.json` holds `"tasks": [{ "id": "...", "text": "..." }]` in the
  order of the list, and `story.md` is not changed by them.
- [ ] **Given** a story with no task, **Then** its `meta.json` has no `tasks` key.
- [ ] **Given** a `meta.json` pulled from GitHub, **Then** its tasks replace the ones here; a task without an id or with an empty text is
  skipped.

## Business rules and constraints

- **A task belongs to one story.** It has an id, given when it is created and kept when its text is edited, and a text. Nothing else (no
  status, no owner, no checkbox) in this story.
- **The order is the order of the list.** A new task goes at the end. Editing does not move a task.
- **Tasks are stored on every change**, like the links, diagrams and UI example of the story. Only the text of the story waits for Save.
- **Tasks are not part of the Markdown.** They live in the story's record in the database and in `meta.json` on GitHub.
- **Only stories have tasks.** Enablers, drivers and ADRs do not.

## Out of scope

- Ticking a task as done, assigning it to someone or estimating it.
- Reordering tasks by drag and drop.
- Undo after deleting a task.
- Writing the tasks back into the `## Tasks` of the text.
- A count of tasks on the Add task button.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `tasks` (id, text, order) to the story in the database, with the endpoint that replaces the tasks of a story.
- [ ] Add the Add task button to the story's `DocumentActionBar`, opening the new-task field of the Tasks section.
- [ ] Build the Tasks section below the text: heading with count, rows with Update and Remove, the shared task form (Enter, Escape, empty
  disabled, trimmed text).
- [ ] Store the tasks on every add, edit and remove, without touching the text or its unsaved changes.
- [ ] Fill the list from `## Tasks` when the story is created, and add the tasks that a saved text gained, without duplicates and without
  bringing back removed ones.
- [ ] Write the tasks into `meta.json` on sync (only when there are some) and read them back on pull, skipping invalid ones.
- [ ] Test adding, editing, cancelling, removing, reloading, the `## Tasks` parsing and the `meta.json` round trip.

tasks.text: Add a `tasks` table (`id UUID`, `story_id`, `text`, `position`) to the database with a Flyway migration script in `bwyn-runtime` (ADR-0010).
Define a `Task` value object and a `TaskRepository` port interface in `bwyn-core` (ADR-0017).
Implement a `ReplaceStoryTasksCommand` and its handler in `bwyn-application` that replaces the full task list for a story (ADR-0017).
Implement the `TaskRepository` outbound adapter using Spring Data JPA in `bwyn-infrastructure` (ADR-0011, ADR-0017).
Add `PUT /stories/{id}/tasks` in `bwyn-rest`, annotated with OpenAPI `@Operation` and `@ApiResponse` (ADR-0014), and a `GET /stories/{id}/tasks` endpoint that returns the ordered list.
Write a `TaskRepositoryIT` Testcontainers integration test verifying persist, replace, and load of tasks (ADR-0012).
Add a `Task` entity model and a `TaskViewModel` in the frontend interface-adapters layer, with a use case that calls `PUT /stories/{id}/tasks` (ADR-0007, AE-0002).
Register the `TaskViewModel` binding in the Inversify composition root (ADR-0006).
Build the `TasksSection` React component in the `ui` layer: heading with count, task rows with pencil and bin, the shared task form (Enter, Escape, empty-disabled, trimmed text) (ADR-0007).
Add the "Add task" button to `DocumentActionBar` for stories only, wired to open the new-task field in `TasksSection` (ADR-0007).

Implement the `## Tasks` parser (use case layer) that extracts top-level bulleted or numbered items under `## Tasks` up to the next heading or horizontal rule, and merges them into the list on story load and on text save without duplicates and without restoring removed tasks.

Implement the sync serialisation: write `tasks` into `meta.json` when the list is non-empty, omit the key when empty; read tasks back on pull, skipping entries without an id or with an empty text (ADR-0048 boundary).

Write Jest tests for `TasksSection`: add, edit, cancel, remove, count, section hidden when empty, only one field open at a time, no artificial delays (Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert).
Write Jest tests for the `## Tasks` parser: bulleted, numbered, with and without checkbox, stops at next heading, no duplicates, removed tasks do not return.
Write a Jest test for the `meta.json` round-trip: serialise tasks, deserialise, skip invalid entries.
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build).

Add a `tasks` table (`id UUID`, `story_id`, `text`, `position`) to the database with a Flyway migration script in `bwyn-runtime` (ADR-0010). _(Done on the existing `story_task` table: `V24__give_story_tasks_an_id.sql` adds the stable `id`, given to existing rows.)_

Define a `Task` value object and a `TaskRepository` port interface in `bwyn-core` (ADR-0017). _(As `StoryTask` in `bwyn-core`; `replaceTasks` is on the existing `StoryRepository` port, like `updateLinks`.)_
Implement the `TaskRepository` outbound adapter using Spring Data JPA in `bwyn-infrastructure` (ADR-0011, ADR-0017). _(In `StoryRepositoryAdapter` with `StoryTaskJpaRepository`.)_

Add `PUT /stories/{id}/tasks` in `bwyn-rest`, annotated with OpenAPI `@Operation` and `@ApiResponse` (ADR-0014), and a `GET /stories/{id}/tasks` endpoint that returns the ordered list. _(As `PUT` and `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/stories/{id}/tasks`.)_
Write a `TaskRepositoryIT` Testcontainers integration test verifying persist, replace, and load of tasks (ADR-0012). _(As `StoryTasksIT`, plus the sync and pull cases in `DocumentSyncIT`.)_

Add a `Task` entity model and a `TaskViewModel` in the frontend interface-adapters layer, with a use case that calls `PUT /stories/{id}/tasks` (ADR-0007, AE-0002). _(`StoryTask` entity, `StoryTasksViewModel`, `ApprovedStoriesUseCase.replaceTasks`.)_

Register the `TaskViewModel` binding in the Inversify composition root (ADR-0006). _(The view model is built in `index.tsx` from `container.resolve(ApprovedStoriesUseCase)`, as the other view models are; the gateway is bound in the composition root.)_

Implement the `## Tasks` parser (use case layer) that extracts top-level bulleted or numbered items under `## Tasks` up to the next heading or horizontal rule, and merges them into the list on story load and on text save without duplicates and without restoring removed tasks. _(Done in the backend domain, which owns the story: `StoryTasks.of` on approval and `StoryTasks.withGained` on every saved text, so the frontend does not parse the Markdown a second time.)_

Implement the sync serialisation: write `tasks` into `meta.json` when the list is non-empty, omit the key when empty; read tasks back on pull, skipping entries without an id or with an empty text (ADR-0048 boundary). _(In `SyncDocument.ofStory` and `SyncDocument.tasksOf`, used by the pull in `DocumentSources`.)_

Write Jest tests for `TasksSection`: add, edit, cancel, remove, count, section hidden when empty, only one field open at a time, no artificial delays (Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert). _(In `story-tasks.acceptance.test.tsx`.)_

Write Jest tests for the `## Tasks` parser: bulleted, numbered, with and without checkbox, stops at next heading, no duplicates, removed tasks do not return. _(As JUnit tests in `ApprovedStoryTest`, since the parser is in the backend.)_
Write a Jest test for the `meta.json` round-trip: serialise tasks, deserialise, skip invalid entries. _(As JUnit tests in `SyncDocumentTest`, since `meta.json` is written and read in the backend.)_
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build). _(`mvn verify` 5m46s plus Jest about 50 s on WSL.)_
